item.title: Professional Portrait Without Changing My Face

turns.text: I'd like a professional headshot, but please keep my face recognisably me. Don't make me younger or smooth away my skin texture. Just tidy up the lighting, outfit and background.

item.tests: Improves professional presentation without beautification that changes facial identity, apparent age or skin texture.

answer_sheet.Face and retouching: Keep my facial proportions, expression, apparent age and natural skin texture. No face reshaping or beauty filter.

must_haves: The face closely matches the source in eye shape, nose, mouth, jawline and facial proportions.
Her apparent age and natural skin texture are retained rather than airbrushed or de-aged.
Her curly dark hair and original expression remain recognisable.
The casual sweater is replaced with a professional outfit.
The park background is replaced with an unobtrusive headshot backdrop, with flattering natural-looking lighting.

turns.text: I'd like you to turn this pic of me into a professional headshot, with just a bit of tidying rather than a whole new look. I always feel a little nervous about edited portraits because I still want to recognise myself when I see the finished image. What matters most, somewhere in all of that, is that you keep my face recognisably me and don't make me younger or smooth away my skin texture. It's really just the lighting, outfit and background that I'd like you to tidy up. I'm hoping this will feel like a more polished version of the photo rather than make me feel like I'm looking at somebody else.
turns.agent:
I couldn't make your headshot. Magic Hour turned down the request because your account doesn't have enough credits, so nothing was created and I have no image to send you.

That attempt was the cheapest option on the free plan, at about 5 credits for one 640px image. The dedicated headshot tool costs 50 credits, so I didn't try it. It also tends to change faces more, which isn't what you want.

The request I set up was written around what matters to you:
- **Keep exactly as is:** your face, expression, age, curly hair, and natural skin texture, including pores and moles. No smoothing, airbrushing or making you look younger.
- **Change only:** the park background to a soft neutral grey studio backdrop, the jumper to a simple navy blazer, and the lighting to even, soft studio light.

**What you can do next:**
1. **Top up credits** in your Magic Hour account (your plan or billing page). A small amount is enough. Then tell me and I'll run the same request again. It'll be a 640px image on the free plan.
2. **Wait for your free credits to renew,** if your plan renews them, and come back to me then.

When it's done, check the face closely. If anything looks less like you, tell me and I'll tighten the instructions before trying again.

approvals.name: edit_image

style.prompt: Turn this photo into a polished professional headshot of the same woman. Keep her face exactly as it is: identical facial features, face shape, eyes, eyebrows, nose, lips, expression, age and natural skin texture including pores, moles and fine detail. Do not make her look younger, do not smooth, airbrush or retouch the skin, do not slim the face or change makeup. Keep her curly dark hair as it is. Only change three things: 1) replace the park background with a clean, softly blurred neutral studio backdrop in warm grey; 2) replace the grey knit sweater with a simple, well-fitted dark navy blazer over a plain crew-neck top; 3) even, soft, flattering studio lighting with gentle key light. Same framing, head-and-shoulders, photorealistic, natural colours.

timeline.text: I'm weighing two options for the headshot: generate_headshot at 50 credits, or edit_image with flux-2-klein at 640px, which is free. The headshot tool tends to regenerate faces, so edit_image with a careful prompt looks like the better bet for keeping the person's identity intact. I'll go with edit_image on the free plan at one image.
